scenarios.given: An existing installation has no workouts and Pro preference; a separate fixture represents a new installation.
scenarios.when: Upgrade both, switch modes around a saved record, and restart during a pending mode change.
scenarios.then: Existing install retains Pro; new install recommends Easy; record IDs/values remain; active presentation stays pinned and requested mode survives restart.

scenarios.given: A clean Easy installation has valid starter data and no active session.
scenarios.when: Open Today and enter each of the three quick-start paths without granting optional permissions.
scenarios.then: All paths are reachable without a routine builder or permission wall; active data fixture instead presents Resume first.

scenarios.given: Pickers contain favorites, repeated recents and a deleted catalog reference.
scenarios.when: Render twice, start a valid recent, then browse/cancel an unavailable choice.
scenarios.then: At most four top choices have stable deduplicated order; one valid start is committed; browsing creates nothing; missing reference has explicit recovery.

scenarios.given: A prepared program workout has linked warm-up/main/cool-down and explicit targets.
scenarios.when: Confirm changed actuals, skip one exercise, interrupt rest and resume, then finish.
scenarios.then: Order/provenance/rest ownership persist; unconfirmed targets are not actuals; skipped work is not completed; existing progression uses only valid program evidence.

scenarios.given: No workout is active and a known machine can be started directly.
scenarios.when: Start it without a routine, finish, then start the same catalog machine again.
scenarios.then: One freestyle workout contains two distinct ordered session-exercise IDs and explicit interval anchors; no planned sets are silently completed.

scenarios.given: A user cannot identify a machine in the catalog.
scenarios.when: Start unnamed exercise, finish it, rename it, then edit its name to whitespace only.
scenarios.then: Start succeeds with stable generic identity; naming is session-local; empty name retains a readable fallback; no catalog creation or history duplication occurs.

scenarios.given: An exercise is running with one recorded set and active rest.
scenarios.when: Finish it twice, open/cancel Next, then send the same next-start command twice.
scenarios.then: Exercise/rest close once; cancel creates nothing; next starts only on explicit command; exactly one next entry exists.

scenarios.given: A new freestyle exercise has no actual reps/load or sets.
scenarios.when: Run for 45 seconds and finish without adding a set; inspect summary and analytics.
scenarios.then: One completed exercise has 45 seconds, zero completed sets and nil reps/load; no volume/PR is created; known-zero and unknown load remain distinct.

scenarios.given: A set-based exercise has configured rest, followed by a duration-only exercise.
scenarios.when: Log a set, continue rest, then finish the exercise and start the duration-only entry.
scenarios.then: Rest records only its own elapsed period; it never completes the exercise; old notifications/callbacks cannot affect the next entry; no new rest is invented.

scenarios.given: No session is active; the preset catalog contains the nine specified stable categories.
scenarios.when: Start each style from its labeled shortcut in isolated fixtures and finish once.
scenarios.then: A count-up timer starts with no mandatory target/link/catalog/permission; exactly one canonical timed activity exists per run with the correct raw style.

scenarios.given: A generic timer is running and external video audio is playing.
scenarios.when: Switch to the video app, lock/unlock and return to WorkoutTracker.
scenarios.then: Timer retains its recording state and elapsed interval; playback is not taken over; video progress/completion does not mutate workout completion.

scenarios.given: An injected clock and isolated store represent a new timer.
scenarios.when: Run 60 seconds, pause 30, resume 20, finish twice and reopen; separately inject backward time and a discontinuity.
scenarios.then: Active duration is 80 seconds with one completion; no negative totals or duplicate intervals; inconsistent recovery requires the specified review instead of invented elapsed time.

scenarios.given: A phone session is paused while a competing quick-start action arrives from another supported surface.
scenarios.when: Cancel conflict, resume existing, then attempt finish-and-start with an injected finish save failure.
scenarios.then: No concurrent new quick start is created; original remains recoverable; failed finish prevents new start; explicit links retain their exact targets.

scenarios.given: A pending transition is assigned a command ID and the store can inject a save failure.
scenarios.when: Fail a start/finish write, retry the same command, and deliver it again with a stale revision.
scenarios.then: No false Saved status, input loss or duplicate record/time/export; at most one committed transition; stale revision is safely rejected.

scenarios.given: A session contains completed work, a running interval and associated rest.
scenarios.when: Finish twice, reopen summary, then apply a permitted history correction; separately finish an empty fixture.
scenarios.then: One summary closes all intervals and notifications; correction recomputes totals/export dirty state; empty/partial work is truthfully labeled and does not inflate records.

scenarios.given: An assigned program and its adherence history exist beside unrelated quick-start activity.
scenarios.when: Complete a duration-only freestyle entry and a generic style timer, then inspect both modes and program progress.
scenarios.then: Quick-start time appears once in history; no fabricated metrics/PR or implicit program advancement; both modes expose the same records.

scenarios.given: Legacy backups, new generic categories, nil metrics and an unsupported raw category are available.
scenarios.when: Migrate, export/restore, delete a catalog source and inspect the persisted records.
scenarios.then: Supported round trips preserve IDs, snapshots, nulls and raw categories; unsupported category never becomes walking; incompatible formats fail explicitly without destructive import.

scenarios.given: A new style has either a reviewed Health mapping or explicitly unsupported export; permission may be denied.
scenarios.when: Finish locally, request supported export, inject failure/retry, then edit after successful export.
scenarios.then: Local record always remains; no guessed GPS/energy/steps; unsupported export is explained; retry is idempotent and edits enter existing reconciliation state.

scenarios.given: Phone, Watch and system surfaces reference a running canonical record.
scenarios.when: Finish from one surface, send a stale action from another, and open a specific guided rest link.
scenarios.then: Surfaces converge without duplicate completion; stale action is safe; rest link resolves exact session and destination in either mode.

scenarios.given: The candidate exposes English/Spanish, large text and VoiceOver layouts with valid recent shortcuts.
scenarios.when: Complete each start path and a next-exercise transition using applicable input/accessibility modes; observe novices.
scenarios.then: Controls remain usable; timer is not announced every second; tap targets and timing goals are measured; at least 4/5 novice completions per applicable path are unaided with correct saved-data understanding.

scenarios.given: A milestone has proposed requirements but no revision-specific product agreement.
scenarios.when: Review its definition of ready and attempt to classify implementation as authorized.
scenarios.then: Implementation remains not started; approval must identify the revised decisions/spec; later changes update intent/scenarios before code.

scenarios.given: Valid proposed/completed manifests and independent invalid fixtures are available.
scenarios.when: Run the validator on duplicate IDs, missing references, cycles, blank assertions and false-completion evidence.
scenarios.then: Valid fixtures pass their mode; every invalid fixture fails with a useful location/diagnostic; planned references are never counted as executed coverage.

scenarios.given: An accepted behavioral change has a mapped scenario and controlled failure fixture.
scenarios.when: Record its failing test before implementation, implement, then run targeted and relevant regression gates.
scenarios.then: The behavioral test passes for the right reason; current-commit evidence and test identity are retained; no disabled assertion or blanket retry hides failure.

scenarios.given: A UI scenario depends on seeded data and launches the host target.
scenarios.when: Run with missing required seed data, then valid data; inspect failure and release evidence.
scenarios.then: Missing data fails clearly in workouttrackerUITestHost; valid fixtures use existing suite patterns; artifacts identify failures and release remains blocked for unmet critical scenarios.
